result:
Good — this is the only `*AgentTest.java` in the project (no other suites affected).

I wrote `src/test/java/org/apache/commons/lang3/text/ExtendedMessageFormatAgentTest.java` with 23 tests covering construction/pattern round-tripping, custom `FormatFactory` lookups (with and without style arguments), fallback to built-in `MessageFormat` types, quoted-literal handling, locale defaulting, `equals`/`hashCode`, the disabled mutator methods, and several malformed-pattern error cases.

22 of 23 tests pass. One fails and shows a real bug:

- **`testTrailingWhitespaceAfterFormatNameIsTrimmed`** — the class Javadoc states that *"format-name and format-style values are trimmed of surrounding whitespace in the manner of `MessageFormat`."* For a pattern like `"{0,upper }"` (a format name with trailing whitespace but no format-style section), `ExtendedMessageFormat.getFormat` only trims the name when a format-style argument is present (`i > 0` branch in `getFormat`); otherwise it uses the untrimmed description `"upper "` as the registry key. The lookup for `"upper "` fails, the format falls through to the built-in `MessageFormat` parser, which doesn't recognize `"upper "` as a type, and the call throws `IllegalArgumentException: unknown format type: upper` instead of resolving the registered `upper` format and producing `"ABC"`.
